notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no Isaiah 22 notes to give you.

The research tool was cut off on my first attempt. I was trying to read the Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary pages for Isaiah 22, and the tool replied that I had no more calls left for this turn. A second, simpler search got the same reply. So I read none of the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. Notes written from memory would break that rule and wouldn't have real URLs behind them, so I've left them out entirely.

If you send the request again in a new turn, the tool should be available, and I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/isaiah-22/, plus the Isaiah 22 pages for Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com/commentaries/, and preceptaustin.org.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly v. 22 (the key of David) and how Eliakim's role points to Christ, especially in connection with Revelation 3:7. I'd search ligonier.org, gty.org, desiringgod.org, wesley.nnu.edu and lcms.org.
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org notes on the hard words, for example "Valley of Vision" in v. 1 and the falling peg in v. 25.
  - bibleodyssey.org on the history behind the chapter.
  - catholic.com and newadvent.org on how Catholics connect v. 22 with Matthew 16:19.
  - Any well-known popular modern teaching on v. 13 ("Let us eat and drink") or v. 22, if the sites discuss it.
